PullRequest.Title: agentHost: fix Keep and Undo getting stuck after forking a chat
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #345857

After a chat was forked, Keep and Undo in the pending file changes bar could fail for good with "another chat in this session also changed it". Each chat of a session records its file edits in its own database, and edits are only ordered within a database. The Working Set treated the latest Keep in database order as covering every chat, and both operations rejected any file that more than one chat had edited.

## Changes

- **Keep is scoped to the chat that recorded it.** A Keep now covers the edits before it in its own chat, and the copies of those edits that a forked chat holds. The new `workingSetSources.ts` decides, per file, which chats still have unkept changes. The Working Set, Keep and Undo all use it.
- **Keep** records in every chat that has unkept records of the file, instead of rejecting the file. Keeping a single hunk needs the unkept changes to come from one chat.
- **Undo** works when one chat has unkept changes to the file, including when another chat's changes to it were kept before. It is still rejected when several chats have unkept changes to the file, which Keep clears. Before it changes the file, a Working Set Undo now checks the file's records in every chat, so it doesn't revert a change that was kept meanwhile.
- **Forks.** Records that a fork only copied from its parent no longer count as the fork's own edits when discarding from the Working Set, Session Changes or Last Turn Changes.
- **Diff across chats.** When several chats have unkept changes to a file, its diff runs from the record that starts them to the record that ends them. Records are matched by the file content they start from and leave, falling back to chat order.
- **Nonce.** A Working Set file's nonce names the last record of every chat with unkept changes. With one chat it is the same as before.
- **Tests.** Cases for each of the above are added to the existing Keep, Undo and Working Set suites. The two Keep cases that asserted the old rejection are replaced.

## Fixes

- Keep and Undo no longer get stuck after forking a chat, both in the issue's steps and when a fork edits a file whose changes were already kept.
- Undo no longer fails after a fork that never touched the file.
- An edit made in one chat after a Keep in another chat is no longer missing from the pending changes, or shown with content the file no longer has.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The exact number of TextDecoder calls follows directly from the added predicate and its two call sites; the old diff shows one decode pair reused. Only magnitude varies with edited-file size and refresh frequency.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU and transient UTF-16 strings allocated by TextDecoder for full-file baseline/current snapshots
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added changed predicate decodes both full snapshots once in `sources.filter(changed)` and again in the second `sources.filter(source => !changed(source))`; a pending file's selected baseline/current are then decoded a third time in computeWorkingSetFiles. Cost scales with total snapshot bytes across every file/source and repeats on each Working Set refresh.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased CPU time and short-lived string allocation/GC delay Working Set updates, especially for multi-megabyte edited files or changesets containing many files.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The removed computeSingleSourceWorkingSetDiff path decoded baseline and current once, compared those strings, and reused them for computeDiffCounts; the fallback similarly decoded only its final endpoints once.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new source classifier converts every source baseline/current to text each time `changed` is invoked, invokes it in both result filters, and does not retain those strings for the final diff call.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 68 introduces uncached full-content decoding used by two separate filters; this replaces deleted code that held `beforeText`/`afterText` and reused them for equality and diff computation.
Findings.Title: Decode each Working Set snapshot only once
Findings.Impact: Even the common single-chat Working Set now performs three pairs of full-file UTF-8 decodes instead of one whenever a file has pending changes. Because observed Working Sets recompute after each tool edit, large files generate repeated large string allocations and slower UI refreshes.
Findings.Evidence: Line 68 defines `changed` via two `toText` calls; lines 70-71 call that predicate independently for pending and unchanged partitioning, and sessionDiffAggregator.ts:440 decodes the chosen baseline/current again before posting them to the diff worker. AgentHostChangesetService refreshes this path after every applied tool edit while subscribed.
Findings.Recommendation: Partition sources in one pass and cache decoded baseline/current text (or use a behavior-equivalent byte comparison for classification), then reuse cached endpoint text for computeDiffCounts so each snapshot is decoded at most once.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The duplicate call path and SQLite query are explicit, and the multi-source trigger is covered by the PR's new cross-chat tests. Exact wall-clock duration depends on file size and edit count, but the doubled query/blob cardinality is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: SQLite BLOB reads and the full-file byte arrays allocated for each before/after snapshot
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a file with E unaccepted records spread across multiple non-held chat databases, computeContents first reads all E snapshots and this line reads all E snapshots again; each snapshot contains whole-file before/after content, so bytes and queries scale as O(E * file size) per pass. Reads for one file/database are serialized by SessionDatabase's per-file sequencer.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Working Set publication incurs excessive database I/O and latency after each tool edit, with additional allocation/GC pressure from loading the same full-file blobs twice.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous Working Set aggregator read each row once when one database held the complete sequence; when no database held all cross-chat rows, it loaded only the first and last snapshots. It did not perform two full row sweeps.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: computeWorkingSetSources now calls computeContents, which loads every candidate row through computeWorkingSetFileContents, and findWorkingSetEnds then maps every row through readStep again whenever there are multiple pending sources or a pending plus unchanged source.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 97 introduces `source.rows.map(... await readStep(...))` after the newly added computeWorkingSetSources pass has already loaded those rows' contents.
Findings.Title: Reuse snapshots instead of rereading every cross-chat edit
Findings.Impact: With the Working Set visible, every applied tool edit queues a full recomputation. If two chats have independently edited the same large file over several tool calls, publishing the refreshed pending-changes UI rereads both full snapshots for every historical row and can visibly lag as history grows.
Findings.Evidence: AgentHostChangesetService.onToolCallEditsApplied refreshes the subscribed Working Set, computeWorkingSetFiles calls computeWorkingSetSources and then findWorkingSetEnds, and SessionDatabase.readFileEditContent executes a SQLite SELECT returning both content BLOBs. computeContents already traverses and reads each source row; added line 97 performs another readStep for every one of those rows on the same critical path.
Findings.Recommendation: Load each record's start/end once and carry a per-source step array or shared `(sourceIdx, record key)` cache from computeContents into findWorkingSetEnds; preserve the current ordering logic while eliminating the second database sweep.

Scenarios.Scenario: Observed Working Set refresh after a tool edits files, including files independently edited in forked chats
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The edit is persisted, AgentHostChangesetService queues computeWorkingSetFiles, all source metadata/content reads and final worker diff must complete before the refreshed Working Set is published. This is the critical path to updated pending-change UI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load all file-edit metadata from every tracked chat database
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getAllFileEdits query per source database per recompute; all historical metadata rows are returned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous unioned Working Set path also loaded all source metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before identities or per-file work can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load full before/after content BLOBs for each candidate edit, then load every row again to order cross-chat endpoints
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For a cross-chat file with E effective non-held unaccepted rows, E reads in computeContents plus E repeated reads in findWorkingSetEnds; pure copied subsets are deduplicated before this point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A holder database's rows were read once; without a holder, only the first and last snapshots were loaded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All reads and endpoint ordering finish before the final diff can be sent to the worker. Same-file reads in one database are serialized by the per-file sequencer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post baseline/current strings to the Node diff worker and await line-diff counts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker call per effective changed file; calls for files are launched together without a separate limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous Working Set aggregator also issued one diff-worker call per effective changed file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each file's result waits for its worker response, and all file promises settle before publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tracked source databases, effective non-held records per file after copy/accept deduplication, edited file byte size, changed-file count, and edit refresh frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refreshes for one owner are sequenced and not-yet-started requests are coalesced. File identity tasks are launched concurrently; source content computations are concurrent, while rows inside computeWorkingSetFileContents are sequential and SessionDatabase serializes same-file operations. The worker receives per-file calls concurrently but processes them through one worker thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no snapshot-content or decoded-text cache across recomputations. The same row can also be fetched twice within one cross-chat computation. Queuing coalesces only refreshes that have not started; a refresh arriving during an active compute queues another full pass.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the refresh call path, SQLite SELECT per read, repeated row sweep, repeated TextDecoder calls, and worker boundary are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical file sizes and cross-chat edit-history lengths vary, but multi-megabyte source files and several tool edits are realistic; exact UI delay is unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff introduces a second full BLOB-read sweep for cross-chat ordering and repeated full-file decoding even in the single-source case.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep all or selected Working Set changes after chats fork
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The operation reads source histories and content, computes pending sources, writes accept records, and only then returns success; range Keep additionally waits for a hunk diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read all edit metadata and candidate content from each tracked source
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata query per tracked source, plus one content query per effective candidate row used by computeWorkingSetSources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Metadata was read across sources, but the operation selected one source and rejected independent cross-chat changes; one source's Working Set contents were computed for range Keep.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before stale-nonce validation and writes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store an accept row transaction and validate the previous row in each pending/unchanged source
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serial transaction per effective source whose records are accepted; each transaction scans metadata and reads the previous content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful Keep stored at most one accept transaction; multi-source independent edits were rejected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Transactions run sequentially and all must finish before success.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute range hunks in the diff worker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for whole-file Keep; one call for a range when exactly one pending source exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Range Keep already used one hunk computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks range Keep while hunks are selected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tracked chat/source count, unaccepted records for the target file, full-file snapshot size, and number of databases requiring accept rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Source metadata reads and accept transactions are serial loops. Content computation across surviving candidates uses Promise.all, but same-file reads in a database serialize. Subsequent Working Set refresh requests are coalesced per owner when queued.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No warm cache is used; rows and content are reread for every operation. Already accepted/copied rows reduce effective candidates, and an empty pending set avoids writes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary counts and serialization; lower concern for impact because each database requires an authoritative accept record.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions normally have few forks, so serial transaction latency is uncertain and lower-severity than the reported repeated snapshot work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: new per-source writes are required to enable the previously rejected cross-chat operation, and source counts are likely modest.

Scenarios.Scenario: Undo Working Set or Session Changes for a file across forked-chat histories
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The operation reads every source's metadata, computes the Working Set source/content, reads/writes the workspace file and records discard rows, revalidates source histories, then optionally accepts unchanged source records before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read metadata/content from tracked and other-chat databases before discard
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full metadata query per tracked source and other-chat database; Working Set Undo additionally reads each effective target-file candidate row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Tracked source metadata was read, but independent multi-source matches were rejected and only the selected source's Working Set content was computed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines whether and how the file may be reverted before filesystem mutation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write/delete the workspace file while applying the revert
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One target file operation sequence per Undo, with work proportional to selected edits/hunks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Undo already performed this file operation sequence for accepted single-source cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The user-visible file change and operation completion wait for it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate all tracked source metadata and store discard/accept records
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata query per tracked source during validation, one discard transaction in the selected source, and up to one serial accept transaction per effective unchanged source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Working Set validation reread only the selected database and did not add accept rows to unchanged sources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Validation and record writes are required before/after completing authoritative Undo.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Source database count, target-file history length, file size, discard step count, and unchanged-source count after deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initial and validation source loops are serial. File edits are coordinated per file; database mutation is transactionally sequenced. Unchanged-source acceptance is also serial.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cross-operation cache. Rows captured before mutation are reused for equality checks, but each database is queried again intentionally for race validation. Copied records are deduplicated when selecting a discard source.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed boundary placement and counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extra metadata scans are usually small compared with file mutation and are necessary for race safety; prevalence of many fork sources is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the extra validation is intentional correctness-critical work, while the avoidable repeated content reads are already reported on the shared Working Set computation path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session Changes diff computation across chat databases
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All source metadata, first/last snapshot reads, and per-file worker diff counts complete before Session Changes are published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load all edit metadata and each identity's first/last content
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata query per source and up to two content reads per effective file identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The refactored helper performed the same metadata and endpoint content reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to construct and count each Session Changes diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post one text pair per changed identity to the diff worker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per effective file after deduplicating copied edit keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All worker responses settle before publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Source count, total metadata rows, deduplicated file identities, and endpoint file sizes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Metadata queries launch together; per-file endpoint reads and worker calls launch concurrently, with one worker thread executing diff work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Full recomputation has no content cache; copied edit identities are deduplicated by key. This behavior is materially unchanged by the refactor.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No changed performance mechanism was identified in this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the refactor preserves effective expensive-boundary cardinality and concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files. Submitted two medium-confidence-impact, high-mechanism-confidence findings: duplicate full BLOB reads in cross-chat endpoint ordering and repeated full-file UTF-8 decoding during source partition/final diff. Keep, Undo, and Session Changes boundaries were traced separately; their remaining added work is required by the new cross-chat semantics or preserves prior cardinality.
